turns.user: What quantitative series do you actually have to forecast dry-bulk rates, and what gaps should I not paper over?
turns.answer:
I ran the live catalog and current prints to answer this from what is actually configured today (as_of 2026-09-09/10), not from what a freight desk would ideally have. Here is the honest inventory and the gaps I will not dress up.

## What is genuinely quantitative and dated on this desk

From the configured market feed (OilPriceAPI reprint, not official Baltic Exchange data):

| Series | Coverage | Latest confirmed |
|---|---|---|
| BDI (Baltic Dry) | daily from 2026-04-10 | 3,620 on 2026-09-09 |
| BCI (Baltic Capesize) | daily from 2026-06-08 | 6,400 on 2026-09-09 |
| Iron ore 62% Fe CFR China | daily from 2026-04-10 | $99.37/t on 2026-09-10 |
| Newcastle thermal coal | confirmed | $147.50/t on 2026-09-09 |
| Coking coal | confirmed | $274.00/t on 2026-09-09 |
| WTI, Brent | 1y/5y daily history confirmed | available |
| VLSFO bunker (Singapore + major ports) | confirmed | available |
| Copper, aluminum, US coal series | confirmed | overlays for Handy/Supramax and Atlantic |

The Cape-side cargo legs (iron ore, coking coal, Newcastle) plus bunker and crude give me a defensible spot-price skeleton for the largest BDI constituent. Broker weeklies (Xclusiv, Intermodal, Banchero Costa), IC Shipbrokers daily color, Baltic weekly recaps, BIMCO SMOO, Clarksons/Geneva Dry, BigMint and Mysteel are all reachable through the press tools and Exa — those are qualitative, dated narratives, not machine-readable series.

## Gaps I will not paper over

1. **BPI, BSI, BHSI are not in the catalog** — confirmed HTTP 404, not a query error. I cannot produce a Panamax, Supramax, or Handysize index level or a dated series for them. The Panamax leg — the demand-side driver for grains and the second-largest BDI constituent — rests on broker commentary and the weekly recap, not a number I can pull. I will not back out a BPI from the composite.

2. **No forward curve, no FFA** — there is no term structure anywhere in my tooling. I can give you spot and a labelled qualitative outlook (SMOO, Clarksons/Geneva Dry), but I cannot give implied forward rates, a carry/roll, or curve positioning. If your desk decision is FFA-relative, that gap is material and I will state it.

3. **No pre-2026 Baltic history** — the feed floor is 2026-04-10 for BDI, 2026-06-08 for BCI, even on a deep key; 2021 and 2025 windows return empty. That kills seasonal and cyclical backtesting from the feed. The plan depth matters too: free is 30 days, Developer 1y, Starter ~5y. I will not reconstruct historical BDI prints from memory.

4. **Not official Baltic Exchange data** — a reprint, sourced as such. If you need audited prints or settlement-grade values, this feed is not that. I will flag the citation status on every figure.

5. **No voyage route rates as a series** — C5, C3, C7, P3A levels exist only as one-off article reads (BigMint, Mysteel, broker PDFs). I cannot pull a clean daily route series, so route-level work is narrative with date-stamped as-of, not a consistent panel.

6. **No supply-side variables in the feed** — orderbook, fleet growth, congestion, eco/scrubber composition are structural drivers I can only source as lagged qualitative items (SMOO, UNCTAD RMT). They are not machine-readable here.

7. **Cross-market as-of alignment** — Baltic prints are London business-day close assessments; iron ore is CFR China on its own timestamp. Pairing them requires explicit as-of labelling, which I do, rather than pretending to a simultaneous quote.

8. **Grains are unconfirmed** in the catalog (wheat/corn/soybean codes are inferred) — I will not lean on them for the Panamax grain leg without confirmation.

## Net position

I can forecast the Cape-driven composite with a real spot skeleton — BDI, BCI, iron ore, coal, bunker, crude — plus dated broker and outlook narratives. What I cannot honestly deliver: a Panamax-level quantitative series, a forward curve, route-rate panels, supply-side data, or pre-2026 backtest depth. If you need any of those as hard series, the right move is bringing in a Baltic-licensed feed or FFA/Clarksons terminal — I will flag where the analysis crosses from sourced numbers into labelled judgement rather than smoothing over it.
